common_scaling_conditional_example.coordinate_transformation_distinction: A time-dependent coordinate rescaling Rphysical=a(t)*r induces shifts and transforms all derivatives/velocities. A genuine coordinate change preserves local observables when every term and observer is transformed. Deleting the hdot term at fixed existing N/beta/gauge registration is not such a transformation.
common_scaling_conditional_example.exact_timelike_zero_shift: At fixed coordinates with beta=0 and fixed lapse, Omega_dot/Omega=-H_s*(2-v^2/cp^2), dln(v)/dt=-H_s*(1-v^2/cp^2), and f=-H_s*v^2/cp^2.
common_scaling_conditional_example.frozen_root_incompatibility_example: With beta=0, fixed g_tt(x), and spatial h=a^2*h0, the instantaneous algebraic radial root has Omega_root proportional to a^-1. The weak-speed conservation tangent at fixed coordinates requires Omega proportional to a^-2. Therefore selecting a new frozen root at every time need not solve one geodesic; radial adjustment or different time evolution is required.
common_scaling_conditional_example.law: h_ij(t,x)=a(t)^2*h0_ij(x), fixed N(x), fixed beta_phi, no meridional shift or twist; H_s=adot/a=partial_t ln rho. This is a spatial scaling, not a full spacetime conformal scaling.
common_scaling_conditional_example.nonrelativistic_zero_shift: At a fixed coordinate radius, conservation gives Omega_dot/Omega approximately -2*H_s; physical axial speed approximately scales as a^-1 and circumferential radius as a.
common_scaling_conditional_example.physical_bound_radius: Constant circumferential radius requires partial_t rho+wA*partial_A rho=0 and its acceleration compatibility. It generally requires nonzero coordinate radial motion in an expanding chart and the full geodesic RHS, not the fixed-coordinate radial-root derivative.
common_scaling_conditional_example.spacetime_conformal_distinction: If the lapse also scales as a, the above fixed-lapse coefficient changes; massive geodesics are not invariant under an arbitrary Weyl transformation. A universal scale interpretation cannot be chosen from a common Omega_dot alone.
common_scaling_conditional_example.timescale_limit: An inverse fractional angular derivative is a local kinematic timescale. It is not an orbital period, escape/disruption time, linear time-to-zero, stability eigenvalue or proven galaxy-age evolution. Applying it through an interval requires the actual metric/material history.
common_scaling_conditional_example.varying_lapse_or_shift: The exact shift form retains beta_dot and f. A source-imposed common hdot factor alone is insufficient to assert an exact -2H law when lapse, shift, twist or actual total hdot differ.

conservation_derivation.assumptions: Neutral constant-mass point tracer obeys the retained S_ordinary[g] geodesic law; t is the registered coordinate time, W=(1,wR,wZ,Omega), u=u^t W. Exact axial Killing conservation additionally requires partial_phi g=0.
conservation_derivation.axisymmetric_instantaneous_evolution: partial_t g_tphi + Omega*partial_t g_phiphi + g_phiphi*Omega_dot + f*J + sum_A(g_Aphi*dot(wA)) = 0, f=dln(u^t)/dt=-Gamma^t_WW.
conservation_derivation.fixed_coordinate_circle: For wA=dot(wA)=0, Omega_dot=-(partial_t g_tphi+Omega*partial_t g_phiphi+f*J)/g_phiphi. This is the axial row in dynamic_circle_residual135, and must also satisfy the meridional rows and normalization along a time interval.
conservation_derivation.general_identity: d(u_phi)/d tau = (1/2)*partial_phi(g_mu_nu)*u^mu*u^nu. This torque identity is retained when represented phi jets are nonzero.
conservation_derivation.instantaneous_zero_meridional_velocity: At wA=0, p_phi=u^t*J with J=g_tphi+g_phiphi*Omega. Its derivative still contains g_Aphi*dot(wA) unless that spatial twist is zero or a persistent coordinate circle has dot(wA)=0.
conservation_derivation.proper_local_velocity: For betaA=h_Aphi=0, rho=sqrt(g_phiphi), v=rho*(Omega+beta_phi)/N and p_phi=rho*Gamma*v. Hence dln(v)/dt=-dln(rho)/dt-dln(Gamma)/dt, with all derivatives along the selected worldline.
conservation_derivation.shift_form_no_meridional_twist: If g_tphi=g_phiphi*beta_phi, Omega_dot=-beta_phi_dot-(partial_t ln g_phiphi+f)*(Omega+beta_phi). Neither Omega nor Omega_dot alone is a normal-observer rotation measurement.
